inline_comments.comment: `TSCONFIG_CANDIDATES` is not exported, yet the identical fallback order (`tsconfig.json` → `tsconfig.base.json` → `tsconfig.app.json`) is duplicated verbatim in both `react-docgen.ts` and `react-docgen-loader.ts`. There is no single source of truth: if a new candidate (e.g. `tsconfig.build.json`) needs to be added later, it must be updated in three separate places and the omission in any one of them would create a silent, hard-to-diagnose behavioral inconsistency between Vite, Webpack, and the manifest codepath. Export this constant and import it in the other two files.

When all three candidates fail and `tsconfigPath` remains `undefined`, the code silently continues with no path-alias resolution. By contrast, `reactDocgenTypescript.ts` (the other consumer of this same fallback logic) now emits an explicit `logger.warn`. Users whose monorepo has no tsconfig variant at all will see path aliases silently fail here without any diagnostic hint. Consider adding a `logger.warn` after the chain — analogous to the one added in `reactDocgenTypescript.ts` — so the failure mode is visible in all code paths.

Same gap as `react-docgen.ts`: when `tsconfigPath` is `undefined` (no tsconfig variant found), the Webpack loader silently falls through with no path-alias resolution and no diagnostic message. A `logger.warn` when `tsconfigPath` is falsy would match the warning behaviour introduced in `reactDocgenTypescript.ts` and give users a consistent experience across Vite and Webpack.

The new `else` branch — which fires when `findTsconfigPath` returns `undefined` — has no unit test. The existing tests in `utils.test.ts` cover `findTsconfigPath` returning `undefined` but they verify that no warning is emitted *from the utility*, not that the caller (`getParser`) correctly emits its own warning in that case. A test that mocks `findTsconfigPath` to return `undefined` and asserts `logger.warn` is called with the expected message would close this coverage gap.

The warning message tells the user to "create a tsconfig.json that extends \"tsconfig.base.json\"" to silence the warning. In many Nx/Turborepo setups the intent is precisely the opposite — `tsconfig.json` is absent on purpose and `tsconfig.base.json` is the canonical root config. Advising users to create a wrapper just to suppress a log entry may cause confusion. Consider instead pointing users toward the Storybook option for explicitly setting a tsconfig path (e.g. `typescript.tsConfigPath` in the main config) so they have a concrete, non-invasive action to take.

general_comments.comment: The PR introduces two separate mechanisms for tsconfig discovery that are kept in sync only by convention. `reactDocgenTypescript.ts` delegates to the cached `findTsconfigPath()` utility (which encapsulates the fallback chain and the warning), while `react-docgen.ts` and `react-docgen-loader.ts` each re-implement the same three-candidate chain inline. If the set of candidates ever needs to change, a developer has to know to update all three sites. A stronger approach would be to export `TSCONFIG_CANDIDATES` from `utils.ts` (or a purpose-built `findTsconfigPath`-style helper that accepts an explicit `cwd`/`projectRoot` pair rather than deriving them internally) and import it wherever the fallback chain is needed.
